candidates.source_name: ATMinfo.si - Stanje bankomatske mreze v Sloveniji
candidates.why_relevant: Independent near-real-time monitor of the Slovenian ATM estate: live count of ATMs (approx 1,046 observed), per-bank availability/uptime percentages for eight banks (NLB, NKBM/OTP, SKB, UniCredit, Addiko, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica, DBS), an interactive ATM map, a searchable ATM list, historical graphs and an alarm feed. It self-declares that its data is sourced from openbanking.bankart.si, i.e. it is effectively a rendered front-end over the national PSD2 ATM-location API. This is the single richest machine-observable view of ATM estate size, per-operator share and geographic coverage for cell 10, and because it is timestamped and refreshed it allows longitudinal tracking of closures rather than only annual snapshots.
candidates.source_subtype: independent monitoring site / ATM estate tracker
candidates.legal_status: unknown - no terms of use inspected; data derived from a third-party open banking API
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic (daily/weekly) scrape of the ATM list and per-bank summary table to build a time series of ATM counts by operator; capture the map/list endpoint payload if a JSON backend exists. Cross-check totals against Banka Slovenije semi-annual payment statistics. Preserve the page timestamp with every snapshot.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on ATM network status, then direct fetch of the site
queries_used: stevilo bankomatov v Sloveniji mreza dvig gotovine Banka Slovenije statistika

candidates.source_name: Bankart Open Banking API Developer Portal (openbanking.bankart.si/hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Bankart is the Slovenian national card/payment processor and the dominant PSD2 hub, marketed as reaching all Slovenian banks through one connection. The developer portal documents APIs that include ATM network data alongside AIS/PIS. Because PSD2 mandates publication of ATM and branch location data, this is the authoritative upstream machine-readable register of ATM locations that ATMinfo.si appears to consume. For a cell about ATM estate and cash access geography, an API returning per-bank ATM coordinates is the highest-value structural asset available - it converts the access-to-cash debate from anecdote into measurable coverage geometry.
candidates.source_subtype: payment processor / PSD2 API hub developer portal
candidates.access_status: portal pages open; API access likely requires developer registration and possibly eIDAS certificates
candidates.legal_status: commercial API terms apply; PSD2 location data is generally publishable without authentication but terms must be read before automated pulling
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Read the portal documentation (node/389 Basic information) to identify the ATM-locator endpoint and whether it is unauthenticated. If open, poll periodically for the full ATM location set; if gated, register as a developer. Treat ATMinfo.si as the fallback rendered view if direct API access is refused.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from the data-source attribution printed on ATMinfo.si
queries_used: openbanking.bankart.si API ATM branch locations PSD2 Slovenia

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije - Statistika: Financne institucije in trgi (payment statistics, ATM and POS series)
candidates.why_relevant: The central bank is the statutory compiler of Slovenian payment statistics under the ECB payments-statistics regulation, published semi-annually with methodological notes. Its releases are the authoritative source for the number of ATMs (e.g. a reported 1,284 at end-H2 2024, down 1.9 percent, with roughly 74 percent contactless-capable), number of POS terminals, card counts by type, and card payment volumes and values. It is also the reference series that press and the legislature quote for the ATM-per-100,000-inhabitants density figure. Any ATM estate model for Slovenia must be anchored on this series.
candidates.legal_status: official public statistics, reuse normally permitted with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Subscribe to the statistics release calendar; on each semi-annual publication download the data series files and the accompanying commentary. Parse ATM/POS/card series into a time series and reconcile with ECB Data Portal payment statistics for Slovenia.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for central bank payment statistics
queries_used: Banka Slovenije placilne statistike bankomati POS terminali polletje podatki
stevilo bankomatov v Sloveniji mreza dvig gotovine Banka Slovenije statistika

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije - Gotovina (cash section: banknotes and coins, cash supply, counterfeits)
candidates.why_relevant: Banka Slovenije organises the supply of banknotes and coins to Slovenia and decides on issuance and withdrawal from circulation. This section carries cash-in-circulation figures, cash supply arrangements, and counterfeit statistics - the demand-side counterpart to the ATM estate. Cumulative net cash issued (reported at 5.61 billion euro from euro adoption to end-2017 in the annual report) and counterfeit withdrawal counts give an independent read on cash usage intensity that is not derivable from card statistics. The central bank's cash department is also the counterparty that accredits cash handlers and recyclers under the Article 6 framework.
candidates.source_subtype: central bank cash operations pages and annual report
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest the gotovina subsection pages and the annual report PDFs; extract the cash-in-circulation and cash-processing chapters each year. Watch specifically for any page listing accredited cash handlers or cash-recycling machine types, which would name CIT and recycler actors.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on cash supply and circulation
queries_used: Banka Slovenije gotovina oskrba z gotovino porocilo bankovci obtok

candidates.source_name: Predlog Zakona o dostopnosti in uporabi placilnih sredstev (ZDUPS) - eUprava e-demokracija public consultation
candidates.why_relevant: The single most consequential live regulatory event for this cell. The Ministry of Finance published the draft ZDUPS on 17 July 2026 (government act ref 2026-1611-0063), public consultation closed 17 August 2026. It was prepared with Banka Slovenije to implement the new Article 74a of the Constitution guaranteeing the right to use cash. Substantively it would oblige credit institutions and Posta Slovenije to maintain a cash-point network with prescribed geographic coverage: an ATM within 5 km of the centre of settlements over 1,000 inhabitants, a branch near settlements over 3,000, a transitional target that by 31 December 2029 at least 90 percent of the population has cash access within 5 km by road, plus a free basic payment package including at least five free out-of-network ATM withdrawals per month. Draft texts and impact assessments in such consultations routinely contain otherwise unpublished coverage statistics and gap maps.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the draft law text and all annexes (obrazlozitev, presoja ucinkov) from the consultation entry; monitor for the post-consultation revised text and the eventual Uradni list publication. Extract every coverage statistic and threshold. Track the successor entry when the bill moves to the National Assembly.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the draft law, snowballed to the consultation portal entry
queries_used: Zakon o dostopnosti in uporabi placilnih sredstev predlog Ministrstvo za finance bankomat 5 kilometrov
e-demokracija predlog zakona dostopnost placilnih sredstev javna obravnava MF

candidates.source_name: Ministrstvo za finance RS (gov.si) - payments and cash accessibility policy
candidates.why_relevant: Sponsoring ministry for ZDUPS and the publisher of the press releases, consultation summaries and post-consultation statements about how many responses were received and which provisions will change. The ministry has already stated publicly that it reviewed the consultation responses in consultation with Banka Slovenije. Ministry communications are where the political framing of the branch/ATM closure debate is set and where the government's own count of cash-access gaps is likely to be first disclosed.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Subscribe to the ministry RSS feed filtered to orgID 24 (already surfaced as a working feed URL) and archive every item mentioning gotovina, bankomat, placilne storitve.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from the ZDUPS consultation coverage
queries_used: e-demokracija predlog zakona dostopnost placilnih sredstev javna obravnava MF

candidates.source_name: Zdruzenje bank Slovenije - GIZ (Bank Association of Slovenia)
candidates.why_relevant: The banking industry's collective voice and the counterparty that pushes back on ATM mandates. ZBS has publicly argued that blanket obligations are disproportionate, that before legislating it is necessary to identify precisely where actual cash-access gaps exist, and has called for clear criteria and data on ATM and branch coverage plus a mechanism obliging all financial service providers - including those without a physical network - to contribute. It has floated ATM redistribution, alternative cash points and cash withdrawal in shops. This is the classic reveals-indirectly source: an industry body arguing against a mandate must produce coverage numbers to make its case.
candidates.access_status: open; some member material may be gated
candidates.legal_status: association publications; check reuse terms for bulletins
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the news/publications section and any Bancni vestnik contributions for ZBS positions and statistics on the branch and ATM network; capture its formal ZDUPS consultation submission if published. Note the association is a strong candidate holder of aggregate member ATM counts not published elsewhere.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the banking association's position on ATM networks
queries_used: Zdruzenje bank Slovenije bankomati mreza poslovalnice gotovina stalisce

candidates.source_name: Euronet EFT Slovenija - independent ATM deployer (Slovenian site)
candidates.why_relevant: Euronet is the principal independent (non-bank) ATM deployer in Slovenia and globally operates roughly 55,000 ATMs across 60+ countries. Its Slovenian commercial site is segmented exactly along this cell's fault lines: a banks/outsourcing page, an explicit 'Bankomati za obcine' (ATMs for municipalities) page targeting the access-to-cash gap left by bank withdrawals, mobile ATMs for events, and internal/off-premise ATMs. The municipalities page is the direct commercial counterpart of the closure debate - it evidences who fills the gaps and on what terms. Euronet is also central to the surcharge controversy (free withdrawals for domestic cardholders ended in February, per press reporting).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Snapshot the product/segment pages (municipalities, banks, mobile, internal ATMs) and any ATM locator; monitor for pricing/surcharge announcements. Complement with Euronet Worldwide SEC filings and quarterly results for the Europe EFT segment ATM counts, which sometimes disclose country-level estate movement.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for independent ATM providers, then site-section snowball
queries_used: Euronet bankomati Slovenija neodvisni ponudnik bankomatov

candidates.source_name: OPSI - Evidenca imetnikov licenc po Zakonu o zasebnem varovanju (register of private security licence holders)
candidates.why_relevant: The definitive machine-readable census of Slovenian CIT operators. The Ministry of the Interior issues and revokes private security licences, and this open-data record contains company name, registered office, business registration number (maticna stevilka), activity code, licence number and TYPE, recorded legal violations, and issuance/revocation dates with current status. Because 'prevoz in varovanje gotovine ter drugih vrednostnih posiljk' is a distinct licence type, the dataset can be filtered to yield the complete legal population of cash-in-transit firms in Slovenia, with entry and exit dates - i.e. structural market data on the CIT segment that no commercial report provides.
candidates.source_subtype: national open data portal dataset / statutory register
candidates.legal_status: open government data, reuse normally permitted under the portal licence - verify the specific dataset licence field
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the dataset resource on a scheduled basis, filter rows by licence type for cash/valuables transport, and diff successive snapshots to detect market entry, exit and revocations. Join on maticna stevilka to AJPES financial statements to size each CIT operator by revenue and headcount.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the CIT licensing regime, snowballed from SPOT permit pages to the open data register
queries_used: register imetnikov licenc zasebno varovanje MNZ prevoz gotovine seznam podjetij
prevoz in oskrba z gotovino podjetja Slovenija varovanje transport denarja

candidates.source_name: SPOT / eVEM - Prevoz in varovanje gotovine ter drugih vrednostnih posiljk (regulated activity and licence pages)
candidates.why_relevant: The authoritative definition of the CIT activity and its licence conditions, and the entry point that names the competent authority (Ministry of the Interior), the licence certificate, and the legal prerequisites (a permanently employed security manager, trained personnel, specially adapted vehicles). It anchors the correct legal terminology for every downstream search and points onward to the licence register, the governing act and the implementing rulebook. Essential for building the cell's glossary correctly rather than searching on colloquial terms.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off harvest for terminology and legal framework; re-check when the private security act is amended. Follow the outbound links to PISRS and the licence register.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on cash transport regulation
queries_used: prevoz in oskrba z gotovino podjetja Slovenija varovanje transport denarja

candidates.source_name: PISRS - Pravilnik o nacinu prevoza in varovanja gotovine ter drugih vrednostnih posiljk
candidates.why_relevant: The implementing rulebook that prescribes HOW cash must be transported and protected in Slovenia - vehicle classes, crew sizes, security-degradation (dye/ink) systems, value thresholds per transport mode. These rules directly determine CIT cost structures and therefore the economics of servicing a rural ATM, which is the hinge of the access-to-cash argument. Amendments to this rulebook are a leading indicator of cost shifts in the cash logistics chain. PISRS is the official consolidated legal register of Slovenia.
candidates.legal_status: official legal text, public domain in substance
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Capture the consolidated text and monitor the PISRS change history for amendments; also track the parent Zakon o zasebnem varovanju (ZZasV-1). Extract value thresholds and crew/vehicle requirements as cost drivers.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on cash transport rules
queries_used: prevoz in oskrba z gotovino podjetja Slovenija varovanje transport denarja

candidates.source_name: Zbornica za razvoj slovenskega zasebnega varovanja (ZRSZV) - private security chamber
candidates.why_relevant: The sector chamber for private security, which runs the statutory further-training programme specifically for cash transport and valuables guarding (izpopolnjevanje za prevoz in varovanje gotovine). Training-programme enrolment, member lists and chamber position papers are an indirect but reliable read on CIT sector size, labour supply and consolidation. Chambers also lobby on rulebook amendments, so their publications surface cost complaints and volume claims from CIT operators that are otherwise unpublished.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest the member directory (if present) to cross-validate the MNZ licence register, and monitor news/position papers on rulebook changes and cash transport economics.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on cash transport training and licensing
queries_used: prevoz in oskrba z gotovino podjetja Slovenija varovanje transport denarja
local_language_terms_used: izpopolnjevanje za prevoz in varovanje gotovine

candidates.source_name: Slovenian CIT operator corporate sites (Sintal, G4S Slovenija, Varnost Vic, FIT varovanje, IBS Varovanje)
candidates.why_relevant: The named actor set for the cash logistics leg of this cell. Sintal describes armed, uniformed CIT crews, satellite vehicle tracking from its monitoring centres, and a cash-degradation system triggered on robbery; G4S Slovenija markets cash transport with anti-robbery escort; Varnost Vic, FIT varovanje and IBS Varovanje all list prevoz gotovine/prevoz denarja among their service lines. Their service pages reveal capability scope (vault services, ATM replenishment, cash processing/recycling) and their client references occasionally identify which banks outsource ATM cash handling - a fact rarely published by the banks themselves.
candidates.legal_status: corporate marketing sites; standard copyright, self-serving claims
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Snapshot each operator's cash-transport and vault/cash-processing service pages; look specifically for ATM replenishment (polnjenje bankomatov), cash centre (denarni center) and recycling capability. Join company identifiers to AJPES annual accounts to size each firm and detect consolidation. Treat marketing claims as claims, not facts.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on named CIT providers, snowballed from the regulated-activity pages
queries_used: Varnost Vic Sintal G4S Loomis Slovenija prevoz gotovine trezor bankomat polnjenje
prevoz in oskrba z gotovino podjetja Slovenija varovanje transport denarja

candidates.source_name: AJPES - business register and annual financial statements (JOLP)
candidates.why_relevant: AJPES holds the Slovenian business register and published annual accounts. Joined to the MNZ licence register by maticna stevilka, it converts the list of licensed CIT firms into a quantified market: revenue, employee counts, ownership and year-on-year trajectory for Sintal, G4S Slovenija, Varnost Vic, FIT and IBS. This is the only practical route to sizing the Slovenian cash logistics market, since no regulator publishes CIT segment revenue. AJPES also publishes payment-transaction statistics (prejemki in izdatki) as a secondary series.
candidates.source_subtype: national business register / financial statements repository
candidates.access_status: largely open for basic register and statements; some bulk/advanced services are paid
candidates.legal_status: official register; bulk reuse may require a paid data service agreement - verify before automated extraction
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Look up each licensed CIT entity by maticna stevilka, pull annual financial statements for a multi-year series, and build a CIT market-size and concentration estimate. Check the terms for automated retrieval before scripting.
candidates.discovered_via_method: inferred as the companion register to the MNZ licence data; surfaced in payment statistics search
queries_used: Banka Slovenije placilne statistike bankomati POS terminali polletje podatki

candidates.source_name: Zdruzenje mestnih obcin Slovenije (ZMOS) - ZDUPS coverage and municipal position
candidates.why_relevant: Municipalities are the aggrieved party in the ATM closure debate and ZMOS is their organised channel into the legislative process. It has published dedicated pages tracking ZDUPS at two separate stages (March 2026 and July 2026), which means it maintains a running institutional record of the bill and of municipal objections. Municipal associations collect member reports of specific closures - place-level detail that never reaches central bank aggregates. The parallel association SOS (Skupnost obcin Slovenije) should be tracked alongside it.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor ZMOS (and search for the equivalent Skupnost obcin Slovenije pages) for ZDUPS-tagged posts and consultation submissions; extract named municipalities reporting closures to build a place-level closure register.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on ATM closures and municipalities
queries_used: zapiranje bankomatov Slovenija dostopnost gotovine obcine

candidates.source_name: Municipal ATM subsidy decisions and council minutes (e.g. Obcina Logatec)
candidates.why_relevant: Where a bank withdraws, some Slovenian municipalities pay to keep an ATM running - reporting indicates Logatec has six ATMs of which the municipality subsidises two, including retaining the ATM in upper Logatec through subsidy. Municipal budgets, council agendas and public procurement notices for such subsidies disclose the actual per-ATM annual cost of rural cash access, a number banks and deployers otherwise treat as commercially confidential. Aggregating these across municipalities yields a bottom-up cost curve for the access-to-cash obligation now being legislated.
candidates.source_subtype: municipal official gazettes, council minutes, budgets, procurement notices
candidates.access_status: open but highly fragmented across ~212 municipal sites
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted search across municipal sites and the public procurement portal (e-narocanje / portal javnih narocil) for tenders and subsidy decisions using terms like 'najem bankomata', 'sofinanciranje bankomata', 'postavitev bankomata'. Start from municipalities named in press coverage, then broaden. Extract contract values and counterparties (often Euronet).
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from press reporting naming Logatec as a subsidising municipality
queries_used: zapiranje bankomatov Slovenija dostopnost gotovine obcine

candidates.source_name: Posta Slovenije - denarne storitve (postal cash access network)
candidates.why_relevant: Posta Slovenije is being written into ZDUPS as a counted node in the national cash-point network, and it already functions as a de facto cash access channel: it offers cash withdrawal over POS terminals to holders of Visa, Maestro, Mastercard, Diners, Discover and Karanta cards, including non-customers of the partner bank. Its treatment of every card transaction on its POS as a cash withdrawal has itself been a public controversy. Post office counts and closures are therefore a second, parallel cash-access estate that must be tracked alongside ATMs - and postal network rationalisation is the same rural-retreat story as bank branch closure.
candidates.source_subtype: state-owned postal operator service pages and annual reports
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Track the money-services pages, the post office locator for network size over time, and Posta Slovenije annual reports for counts of postal units and cash transaction volumes. Cross-reference with AKOS universal postal service reports on network coverage obligations.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on postal cash withdrawal and cashback
queries_used: Posta Slovenije dvig gotovine dostop bankomat cashback trgovine Slovenija

candidates.source_name: Bank ATM and branch locator pages (NLB, OTP banka, UniCredit Bank Slovenija, Delavska hranilnica, SKB, Addiko, Sparkasse, DBS)
candidates.why_relevant: Each bank publishes its own branch and ATM locator, which is the primary-source ground truth for that operator's estate and the raw material behind PSD2 aggregation. Diffing locator contents over time detects individual site closures at address level before any aggregate statistic reflects them, and the per-bank split lets you attribute the national decline to specific institutions. Delavska hranilnica and UniCredit locators were both surfaced in local-language search; ATMinfo's per-bank table confirms the eight-bank universe.
candidates.domain: otpbanka.si, nlb.si, unicreditbank.si, dh.si, skb.si, addiko.si, sparkasse.si, dbs.si
candidates.access_status: open; locators are often JS-driven with an underlying JSON endpoint
candidates.legal_status: corporate sites; check robots.txt and terms before systematic scraping
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the Bankart PSD2 aggregate over per-bank scraping; use per-bank locators for validation and for banks missing from the aggregate. Where a locator has a JSON backend, capture it on a monthly cadence and diff by address to build a closure event log. Respect robots.txt.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for ATM networks, plus the bank list exposed on ATMinfo.si
queries_used: stevilo bankomatov v Sloveniji mreza dvig gotovine Banka Slovenije statistika
Zdruzenje bank Slovenije bankomati mreza poslovalnice gotovina stalisce

candidates.source_name: Slovenian business and general press covering ATM closures and cash access (Delo, Forbes Slovenija/N1, RTV SLO, Svet24, Zurnal24, Domovina, Lider.si)
candidates.why_relevant: The press is where otherwise-unpublished numbers surface, because regulators, ministers, ZBS and municipalities argue in public. Concrete figures already extracted from this layer include: 1,304 ATMs of credit institutions and independent providers at end-2025; density of 61.1 ATMs per 100,000 inhabitants against a proposed statutory minimum of 60; a 30 percent decline in ATM numbers since 2011 concentrated in rural areas; the branch network halved over fifteen years with roughly 450 ATMs removed; and 91 percent of the population within 5 km of cash at end-2025 against a 90 percent target for 2029. Domovina is running a multi-part ZDUPS dossier; RTV SLO carried the supervisor Dolenc warning banks to preserve payment and cash infrastructure.
candidates.domain: delo.si, forbes.n1info.si, rtvslo.si, svet24.si, zurnal24.si, domovina.je, lider.si, maribor24.si, slo24.si, nadlani.si, info360.si
candidates.access_status: mostly open; Delo and some titles apply metered paywalls
candidates.legal_status: copyrighted journalism - index and quote briefly with attribution, do not republish full text
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Standing keyword alerts in Slovenian across these domains on: zapiranje bankomatov, ukinitev bankomata, dostop do gotovine, bancne poslovalnice, ZDUPS. Extract quantitative claims into a fact register with the attributed original source (usually Banka Slovenije or ZBS) so figures can be traced back to primary data.
candidates.discovered_via_method: both local-language searches; heavy snowballing across titles

candidates.source_name: Uradni list Republike Slovenije (Official Gazette)
candidates.why_relevant: The point of legal truth for when ZDUPS and any amendments to the private security rulebook actually enter into force, and the publisher of an explanatory note on ZDUPS regulating the right to use cash and to pay electronically at points of sale. Municipal official gazettes are also published here in part, which can capture municipal ATM subsidy decisions. Needed to distinguish draft proposals from binding obligations - a distinction that matters greatly when the whole cell hinges on whether coverage mandates become law.
candidates.access_status: open for the gazette; some commentary services are subscription
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor for publication of ZDUPS and of amendments to ZZasV-1 and the cash transport rulebook; archive the final texts and effective dates.

candidates.source_name: OZS - Obrtno-podjetniska zbornica Slovenije (Chamber of Craft and Small Business) - ZDUPS consultation response
candidates.why_relevant: The small-business chamber is the merchant-side stakeholder in the cash debate: its members both accept cash (and therefore need deposit access and CIT services) and would be obliged under ZDUPS to accept at least one electronic payment method. Its consultation commentary and zastopanje (advocacy) pages capture merchant complaints about cash deposit costs, branch closures affecting daily takings, and card acceptance costs - the merchant-facing half of the cash-access ecosystem that bank-side sources omit.
candidates.access_status: open; some member content may be gated
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the news and zastopanje sections for cash and payment-related positions; capture the formal ZDUPS submission.

candidates.why_relevant: A third-party aggregator that enumerates Slovenian banks and their PSD2 API endpoints. Useful as a shortcut to the full set of per-bank developer portals, each of which is obliged to expose ATM and branch location data, giving an independent path to the ATM estate if the Bankart hub proves gated. candidates.source_name: Academic and student theses on cash transport and ATM security in Slovenia (e.g. academia.si diploma on comparison of cash transport and protection)
candidates.why_relevant: Slovenian diploma and masters theses on private security routinely compare CIT providers, describe operational practice, and reproduce operator-supplied data (fleet sizes, route economics, ATM servicing frequency) that companies will not disclose to a researcher directly. They also cite the regulatory framework precisely. Combined with the national repository, this is an underrated route to CIT operational detail. The national aggregator repozitorij.uni-lj.si / dKUM and the Univerza v Mariboru Faculty of Criminal Justice output should be swept alongside this single example.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Search Slovenian institutional repositories for prevoz gotovine, varovanje gotovine, bankomat varnost; extract company-level operational detail and treat figures as dated and indicative rather than current.

negative_findings.description: No evidence was found of Loomis, Brink's or Prosegur Cash operating a Slovenian cash-in-transit subsidiary. A targeted Slovenian-language search naming Loomis alongside domestic providers returned only domestic firms (Sintal, G4S Slovenija, Varnost Vic, FIT varovanje, IBS Varovanje) and no international CIT specialist other than G4S.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Slovenian CIT market appears to be served by domestic private security firms plus G4S, with no visible presence of the global pure-play CIT majors. This is a hypothesis based on absence in search results, not a verified market fact.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Market structure and consolidation prospects for cash logistics differ sharply depending on whether global CIT majors are present. If confirmed, the Slovenian CIT segment is a domestic-security-firm market where cash transport is one service line among many, rather than a specialist cash-handling industry - which affects pricing, cash-centre investment and willingness to invest in recycling technology.

negative_findings.description: No source was found that publishes Slovenian ATM WITHDRAWAL VOLUMES or VALUES at ATM, operator or geographic level. Banka Slovenije payment statistics coverage surfaced in search focused on ATM counts, card counts and card payment volumes; the ATM-cash-withdrawal series was not confirmed as separately published, and no per-operator or per-municipality withdrawal data appeared in any local-language search.
negative_findings.result_summary: Estate counts are well covered; cash withdrawal throughput is not. The withdrawal side is presently only inferable from cash-in-circulation aggregates.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal counts alone cannot distinguish a shrinking but heavily used ATM estate from a shrinking and lightly used one. Without withdrawal volumes, the commercial case for or against maintaining rural ATMs - and the addressable market for deployers and CIT firms - cannot be sized. This gap should be attacked next via the ECB Data Portal payment statistics for Slovenia, which does carry ATM withdrawal series.

negative_findings.description: Searching did not surface a settled Slovenian term or any identified actor for CASH RECYCLERS or cash-recycling ATMs (candidate terms would be 'recikliranje gotovine', 'bankomat z vplacilom', 'vplacilni bankomat', 'depozitni bankomat', 'denarni center'). No Slovenian vendor, bank programme or Banka Slovenije accreditation list for cash recycling was found in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: The cash-recycler sub-topic of this cell is currently uncovered: neither terminology nor actors were confirmed in Slovenian.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Recycling ATMs materially change CIT servicing frequency and the cost of rural cash access, which is precisely the variable the ZDUPS coverage mandate turns on. A blind spot here means the cost side of the access-to-cash obligation cannot be modelled. Explicitly flagged as a local-language coverage failure, per the mandatory-local-language rule.

negative_findings.description: The Bankart open banking hub's ATM-network API was identified from portal documentation summaries but the actual endpoint, its authentication requirements and its terms of use were NOT inspected. It is unknown whether the ATM locator is unauthenticated (as PSD2 location data usually is) or requires developer registration and eIDAS certificates.
negative_findings.result_summary: High-value machine-readable source identified but access conditions unverified. Not a failure - an open verification task.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Whether this API is openly pollable determines whether the entire ATM estate can be tracked directly and lawfully, or whether the pipeline must depend on the third-party ATMinfo.si rendering with its unknown terms and unknown completeness (ATMinfo showed ~1,046 ATMs against ~1,284-1,304 reported by Banka Slovenije, suggesting it may not cover independent deployers such as Euronet).

negative_findings.description: Three different ATM totals were observed and are not reconciled: ATMinfo.si displayed 1,046 ATMs across eight banks; press citing Banka Slovenije reported 1,284 at end-H2 2024 (down 1.9 percent); and other reporting cited 1,304 at end-2025 for credit institutions AND independent providers combined.
negative_findings.result_summary: The gap of roughly 250 units is most plausibly the independent-deployer estate (Euronet and similar) absent from the bank-only aggregation, but this was not verified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The independent deployer share of the Slovenian ATM estate may be around 20 percent - materially larger than the bank-centric debate implies - and directly determines who the commercial counterparties are for ATM hardware, servicing and cash logistics. Reconciling these three series is a priority analytical task and would itself be a finding.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenian trade association specifically for independent ATM deployers or for the ATM industry was found (no national equivalent of an ATM Industry Association chapter surfaced in either language). Euronet appears to engage the market and municipalities directly rather than through a sector body.
negative_findings.result_summary: The independent deployer segment has no organised collective voice in Slovenia that could be tracked as a single source.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absent a trade body, deployer-side data and lobbying positions must be gathered actor by actor (chiefly Euronet, plus its parent's investor disclosures) and from municipal procurement records, which is more labour-intensive and less complete. It also means the ZDUPS consultation record may under-represent the deployer perspective.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash recycling and automated cash deposit infrastructure in Slovenia is entirely uncovered - no terminology, vendors, bank deployments or central bank accreditation lists were identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated Slovenian-language pass on 'vplacilni bankomat', 'depozitni bankomat', 'bankomat z vplacilom gotovine', 'recikliranje gotovine', 'denarni center'; check Banka Slovenije's cash pages for any register of accredited cash handlers under the Eurosystem framework for banknote recirculation; and check hardware vendor country pages (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, GRG, Sigma/CIMA distributors) for Slovenian references.

coverage_gaps.description: ATM withdrawal volumes and values, and any geographic breakdown of cash withdrawal activity, were not located in national sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Query the ECB Data Portal payment statistics for Slovenia (ATM withdrawal number and value series) and the Banka Slovenije statistical data series files directly rather than relying on the press summaries; also check the annual ECB SPACE study for Slovenian payment-behaviour shares of cash at point of sale.

coverage_gaps.description: ATM hardware, software and managed-services vendors serving the Slovenian estate were not investigated at all in this pass - only deployers, banks and CIT firms were mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search Slovenian public procurement (portal javnih narocil / e-narocanje) for bank and municipal ATM tenders to identify supplying vendors and contract values, and check regional distributor and integrator sites. Bank tenders are a reliable route to vendor identity and estate refresh cycles.

coverage_gaps.description: Public procurement records were identified as the likely richest untapped source for both municipal ATM subsidies and bank ATM/CIT contracts, but were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically query the Slovenian public procurement portal for 'bankomat', 'prevoz gotovine', 'varovanje in prevoz gotovine' to extract contracting authorities, winning bidders, contract values and durations - the only public route to per-ATM and per-route cost data.

coverage_gaps.description: The individual written responses to the ZDUPS public consultation (closed 17 August 2026) were not retrieved - only third-party reporting on ZBS's and OZS's positions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the eUprava consultation entry (id 19166) and the Ministry of Finance pages for the published response file or the ministry's summary of comments; request the responses if not published. These filings are the densest likely concentration of unpublished ATM and branch coverage data in the entire cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Only one subsidising municipality (Logatec) was identified by name; the population of Slovenian municipalities that subsidise or tender for ATMs is unknown, and there is no consolidated register of ATM closure events at settlement level.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a closure and subsidy event register by sweeping regional news outlets (maribor24, slo24, nadlani and other regional titles), the two municipal associations ZMOS and SOS, and municipal council minutes; geocode events to compare against the ZDUPS 5 km coverage test.

brief: Slovenia's ATM and cash-access source landscape is unusually rich right now because a constitutional right to use cash (Article 74a) is being implemented through the draft Zakon o dostopnosti in uporabi placilnih sredstev (ZDUPS), whose July-August 2026 public consultation has forced Banka Slovenije, the bank association ZBS, municipalities and merchants to argue with numbers in public. The estate itself is exceptionally observable: Banka Slovenije semi-annual payment statistics give the authoritative counts (around 1,284-1,304 ATMs, a 30 percent decline since 2011, 61.1 per 100,000 inhabitants), while the Bankart PSD2 open-banking hub and its rendered front-end ATMinfo.si expose near-real-time per-bank ATM locations, counts and uptime - making address-level closure tracking technically feasible. The cash logistics leg is mapped through regulation rather than commerce: the MNZ private-security licence register on the national open data portal yields the complete legal population of CIT operators (Sintal, G4S Slovenija, Varnost Vic, FIT, IBS), which joined to AJPES accounts allows the segment to be sized, with no global CIT major evident beyond G4S. The principal blind spots are withdrawal volumes, cash recycling infrastructure (for which no Slovenian terminology or actor could be established), and the unretrieved ZDUPS consultation filings and municipal ATM procurement records, which are the likeliest repositories of otherwise unpublished coverage and cost data.
